purpose: M4-flavored retest: OpenVINO master vs the working 2026.5 snapshot on this machine

stack_under_test.build: isolated worktrees ~/AI/src/openvino-master and ~/AI/src/openvino.genai-main; wheel installed to ~/AI/install/openvino-master-test; working installation untouched

results.gpu_sanity: PASS - greedy generation works on the plain stateful path

gpu_perf_qwen3-1.7b.verdict: master measured ~2x slower decode and ~4x TTFT on a single-run probe; gap far exceeds run-to-run noise

details: master no longer builds the NPU compiler in-tree; it downloads a prebuilt VCL compiler for Ubuntu 22.04/24.04/26.04 ONLY - Fedora 44 is explicitly skipped ('Can not use plugin compiler libraries')
with IE_NPU_COMPILER_TYPE=PLUGIN the build without compiler libs falls back to the broken driver compiler (ZE_RESULT_ERROR_UNKNOWN 0x7ffffffe, vclAllocatedExecutableCreate2)

after spoofing lsb_release=Ubuntu 24.04 during configure, the prebuilt compiler v8.5.0 (436452c, sha256-verified by cmake) was fetched and installed into the wheel libs; NPU compilation STILL fails with the same vclAllocatedExecutableCreate2 error
the known-good control (qwen3-0.6b-int4, compiles in seconds on the 2026.5 snapshot) fails on master => master cannot use this NPU at all

results.packaging: the master wheel still omits libopenvino_intel_npu_compiler*.so and libopenvino_intel_npu_vm_runtime.so; the symlink/copy workaround remains necessary
results.abi: GenAI 2026.5 does not load against OV master (SDPAToPagedAttention signature changed) - full-stack upgrades must move together

conclusion: The latest code is NOT better on this machine: worse on GPU (measured), broken on NPU (Fedora unsupported + vcl failure persists with the prebuilt compiler). The 2026.5 snapshot remains the correct stack. Re-test before any upstream upgrade; do not assume newer is better.
